definitions.full: H2767. Chormah חָרְמָה proper name, of a location ( asylum , compare Arabic id. , Wetzst ZKW see 1884, 115) — a royal city of Canaanites, in the South, in tribe of Simeon Num 14:45 (J E; article only here see Di), 21:3 (J) where name explanation from Israel's devoting Canaanites of Arad to destruction; Josh 15:30 ; 19:4 (P), Deut 1:44 ; Josh 12:14 (D), 1Sam 30:30 ; 1Chr 4:30 ; originally called צְפַת Judg 1:17 , where name is said to have been changed to Hormah because Judah and Simeon (after death of Joshua) devoted its inhabitants to destruction, see Di Num 21:3 . — On site see צְפַת .

occurrences.englishText: Then the Amalekites came down, and the Canaanites who lived in that mountain, and struck them and beat them down, even to Hormah.
Yahweh listened to the voice of Israel, and delivered up the Canaanites; and they utterly destroyed them and their cities. The name of the place was called Hormah.* “Hormah” means “destruction”.
The Amorites, who lived in that hill country, came out against you and chased you as bees do, and beat you down in Seir, even to Hormah.
Judah went with Simeon his brother, and they struck the Canaanites who inhabited Zephath, and utterly destroyed it. The name of the city was called Hormah.
